children: added more than 30% in the premarket on Tuesday after disclosing that its GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist VK2735 delivered 22% weight loss and showed potential in maintaining weight loss effects with less frequent dosing regimens.

Citing topline data from its VK2735-102 maintenance study, the company said that the injectable, as a once-weekly therapy, caused approximately 16% - 19% weight loss compared with roughly 0% for placebo over 21 weeks in the induction phase of the study.

During the 12-week maintenance phase, patients who moved to every-other-week and monthly dosing regimens maintained up to 97% and 90% of the average weight loss during the induction period, respectively, compared with 61% of the average weight loss maintained in the placebo group.
According to the company, patients receiving 17.5 mg VK2735 weekly recorded 22% of placebo-adjusted weight loss over the 33 weeks of the study.

As for safety, one participant discontinued the study during the induction period due to an adverse event. The company noted one trial discontinuation in each group of patients who transitioned from a weekly to an every-other-week regimen and from weekly to monthly dosing due to adverse events during the maintenance phase.
